_README_COMMENTS: Keys starting with '_' are comments/documentation and are ignored by the generator.
_README_USAGE: Edit case_name, stl_files, and flow conditions. All other fields use robust built-in defaults.
_stl_files: ASCII STL geometry files located in the stl/ directory
_fidelity: Preset resolution: 'fast' (iteration), 'standard' (recommended), 'fine' (report). Cell size scales with the model: each preset meshes 'cells_per_length' cells along the longest bounding-box dimension (20/30/37.5 -> 0.15/0.10/0.08 m on a 3.0 m car), so a 1.2 m front wing is meshed proportionally finer than a full car at the same relative cost. The cell count also depends on the mesher: a 'standard' Formula Student car produced ~0.45M cells with snappy and ~4.4M with cfMesh. Pin the old absolute behaviour with mesh_params.base_cell_size (metres), retune the scaling with mesh_params.cells_per_length, and read 'cells:' from log.checkMesh after the first run.
_mesher_comment: Mesher engine: 'cfmesh' (robust boundary layers) or 'snappy' (classic multi-stage). Engine-specific knobs live in src/rapidfoam/mesher_profiles/<mesher>.json (overridable per project in configs/meshers/<mesher>.json). The same case file can drive either engine: rapidfoam -c configs/config.json --mesher snappy

flow._velocity_comment: Freestream air velocity in m/s (16.67 m/s ≈ 60 km/h, 20.0 m/s = 72 km/h)
flow._direction_comment: Flow direction vector: +x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z (direction the air travels)
flow._ground_comment: true = moving ground wall at freestream velocity; false = slip wall (free-air aero)

outputs._drag_axis_comment: Axis along which aerodynamic drag is reported (direction of freestream flow)
outputs._downforce_axis_comment: Axis along which downforce (-lift) is reported (-y = toward ground, +y = aircraft lift)

_domain_box_comment: 'auto' automatically fits wind tunnel around STL (4L upstream, 8L downstream, 4H top, 4W lateral). Or provide explicit {'min': [x, y, z], 'max': [x, y, z]}.
_symmetry_plane_comment: Centerline coordinate if model uses a symmetry plane (0.0 if centered at origin, or specify offset if origin is shifted). Omit if full 3D model.
_ground_position_comment: Optional ground elevation control (delete leading '_' from ONE key below to activate; omit both to snap to lowest STL vertex):
_ground_clearance_desc: Style 1 (Relative): Gap in meters below lowest STL point (e.g. 0.035 = 35mm ground clearance / ride height)
_ground_plane_desc: Style 2 (Absolute): Fixed CAD coordinate of ground / road elevation (e.g. 0.0 if geometry is positioned relative to origin)
_domain_faces_comment: Boundary types for the 6 outer box faces (-x, +x, -y, +y, -z, +z). Available types: inlet, outlet, ground, farField, symmetry.

parallel._comment: Number of CPU cores for MPI decomposition, meshing (cfMesh cartesianMesh via cfmesh.parallel_meshing, or snappyHexMesh) and simpleFoam solving. cfMesh takes its rank count from system/decomposeParDict, so keep this equal to the SLURM --ntasks.

slurm._comment: SLURM cluster configuration for HPC / compute cluster

_overrides_note: All fields below have built-in defaults in the fidelity presets plus the mesher profile. Uncomment only if manual tuning is needed.
_mesher_blocks_note: See docs/meshers.md for what each engine means by a key. Anything the two engines read differently is expressed in mesh_params_<mesher> (this case only) or configs/meshers/<mesher>.json (whole project). cfMesh-native: min_cell_size (its automatic-refinement floor, 'body' by default) plus the cfmesh block (feature_angle, ground_refine, ground_cell_size, boundary_cell_size, refinement_thickness, optimise_layer, optimisation, parallel_meshing). snappy-native: nCellsBetweenLevels, maxGlobalCells, distance_levels/distance_shells. Both engines: body_cell_size/edge_cell_size in metres, surface_level/edge_level (cfMesh derives its body and edge cells from them), base_cell_size ('auto' = the preset's cells_per_length x the longest bounding-box dimension), cells_per_length, refinement_regions, the wake-level keys (wake_levels_below_surface, or an absolute near_wake_level/far_wake_level) and trailing_edge_refine/te_level/te_height_cells/te_depth_cells (the local trailing-edge box, on by default). rapidfoam validate names any key the selected engine does not read.

mesh_params_cfmesh._te_note: Trailing-edge refinement is ON by default in every fidelity preset: one box (objectRefinements/trailingEdgeBox) on the trailing-edge plane at base_cell_size / 2**te_level, because cfMesh's automatic refinement is capped by min_cell_size, so a trailing edge thinner than the body cell (a 1.4 mm wing trailing edge against a 6.25 mm cell) would stay slivery. Set trailing_edge_refine false to drop it, keep te_level 'auto' (= edge_level + 1) unless a specific trailing-edge gap needs resolving. Verify with: grep -A6 trailingEdgeBox system/meshDict

mesh_params_snappy._wake_note: Wake boxes are sized as fractions of the model and their levels sit this many levels below surface_level[0] ([near, far]), so the wake keeps its share of the mesh when the surface level or the model size changes. State near_wake_level / far_wake_level for an absolute level. Every run prints a cell-budget estimate per region and warns when the regions approach maxGlobalCells, because snappy stops refining once the cap is hit: grep 'Cell budget' or read it above 'Case:'.

mesh_params._base_cell_size_desc: Absolute override in metres (e.g. 0.10 to reproduce the pre-1.2 car-scale presets). 'auto' = cells_per_length x the longest bounding-box dimension, which is the default.
mesh_params._cells_per_length_desc: Auto-size knob: 20 fast / 30 standard / 37.5 fine background cells along the model's longest bbox dimension. Raise it to resolve a front wing or a subassembly at the same preset.
mesh_params._min_cell_size_desc: cfMesh's global refinement floor: 'body' (default), 'edge' (resolves flap slots and trailing edges everywhere; measured 1.82M -> 3.95M cells on the test body), 'base', or metres.
mesh_params._distance_shells_desc: Distance shells in units of the base cell (multiple x base_cell_size -> level); use distance_levels for absolute metres.
